title: Vision AI in 2025 — Peter Robicheaux, Roboflow

summary: Peter Robicheaux, ML lead at Roboflow, argues that computer vision remains critical because systems interacting with the physical world require vision as a primary input, with a larger gap between human and computer vision than exists for speech. Vision problems are distinct from LLM problems: latency usually matters, multiple frames per second are needed for motion perception, and edge deployment is typically required. He identifies several problems with the vision field in 2024. First, vision evals like ImageNet and COCO are saturated and mostly measure pattern matching rather than visual intelligence. Second, vision models don't leverage big pre-training the way language models do—Claude 3.5 and Claude 4 cannot tell time from a watch image, and ChatGPT-4o cannot identify which direction a school bus is facing, hallucinating details to support wrong answers. The MMVP dataset demonstrates this by finding image pairs close in CLIP space but far in DINOv2 space, showing CLIP's contrastive training fails to capture discriminating visual details. DINOv2, a self-supervised pure vision model, discovers meaningful PCA features and object segments without language supervision. The distinction between convolutional and transformer models explains why pre-training hasn't helped: YOLOv8 gains only 0.2 mAP from Objects365 pre-training while LW-DETR gains 5-7 mAP. Roboflow announces RF-DETR, which swaps the LW-DETR backbone for DINOv2, achieving decent COCO improvements and massive gains on their new RF100VL benchmark by leveraging stronger embeddings. RF100VL comprises 100 hand-curated datasets from Roboflow Universe covering difficult domains like aerial views, microscopes, and X-rays, with data sourced from researchers who use Roboflow's free platform and contribute data back as open source. The benchmark is publicly available at rf100vl.org with code utilities and on Hugging Face. Its few-shot tract provides canonical 10-shot splits with class names, annotator instructions, and 10 visual examples per class. No model can leverage all three inputs better than using just one, highlighting a key VLM shortcoming. Specialist models currently perform best: zero-shot grounding DINO achieves 19 mAP, YOLOv8 nano trained from scratch on 10-shot examples gets 25 mAP, and fine-tuned grounding DINO with federated loss is the highest performing model on the dataset. RF-DETR's smallest size is 20 million parameters, enabling edge deployment.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: Why Computer Vision Matters
sections.summary: Peter Robicheaux introduces himself as ML lead at Roboflow and argues computer vision matters because real-world systems need visual input, with latency and edge deployment being key constraints distinct from LLM problems.

sections.title: Problems with Vision in 2024: Saturated Evals and Dumb Models
sections.summary: Identifies saturated vision evals (ImageNet, COCO measure pattern matching not intelligence), vision models not leveraging big pre-training like LLMs, and demonstrates model blindness via Claude failing to read watch times and MMVP dataset showing ChatGPT-4o failing on school bus orientation.

sections.title: CLIP vs DINOv2: Vision-Language Pre-training Failure
sections.summary: Explains MMVP methodology: finding image pairs close in CLIP space but far in DINOv2 space reveals CLIP's contrastive training fails to capture discriminating visual details. DINOv2's self-supervised pre-training discovers meaningful PCA features and object segments without language supervision.

sections.title: Convolutional vs Transformer Pre-training and RF-DETR Announcement
sections.summary: Shows YOLOv8 gains only 0.2 mAP from Objects365 pre-training while LW-DETR gains 5-7 mAP, demonstrating transformers leverage pre-training better. Announces RF-DETR using DINOv2 backbone with improvements on COCO and massive gains on RF100VL.

sections.title: RF100VL Benchmark Introduction
sections.summary: Introduces RF100VL, 100 hand-curated datasets from Roboflow Universe covering difficult domains like aerial, microscopes, and X-rays. As a vision-language benchmark, it reveals YOLOv8 with 10 examples/class beats Qwen2.5-VL-72B, showing VLMs struggle with visual distribution shifts despite strong linguistic generalization.

sections.title: Q&A: Edge Deployment, Availability, and Benchmark Details
sections.summary: Covers RF-DETR edge deployment (20M parameters at smallest), RF100VL public availability at rf100vl.org with code and Hugging Face, Roboflow's free-researcher platform strategy with open-source data contribution, RF100VL's few-shot tract with 10-shot splits providing class names, annotator instructions, and visual examples, and specialist model benchmarks: zero-shot grounding DINO at 19 mAP, YOLOv8 nano from scratch at 25 mAP, and fine-tuned grounding DINO with federated loss as the top performer. Notes no model leverages all three few-shot inputs better than one alone, highlighting VLM shortcomings.
